clue.text: Boorish type sitting in train, not in horse-drawn carriage

indicators.note: the boorish type is seated inside the shortened word, so one piece goes within the other
not in says the two letters of in are dropped from the word train

parts.note: taken as written, the letters removed
an oik is British slang for an uncouth, boorish person

explanation.surface: A loutish passenger on a train is unwelcome in a carriage pulled by horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian vehicle drawn by a team of three horses abreast.

clue.text: Brief visit to sailing boat, say, in old port abroad

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter of the word for a visit is dropped

parts.note: to call is to pay a visit

indicators.note: say signals that the boat's name is spoken, giving a sound rather than a spelling

parts.note: a cutter is a small single-masted sailing vessel

explanation.surface: A quick trip out to a yacht, perhaps, in some historic harbour overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the boat's name ends in an unsounded R, so it is heard as CUTTA, the ending of the Indian city's old spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The former name of Kolkata, an Indian seaport long under British rule.

clue.text: Evaluate performance of dunces at school

parts.note: asses are fools or dunces

explanation.surface: A teacher is told to judge how the class duffers are doing.
explanation.definitionFit: To appraise or judge how well something has been done.

clue.text: Record American senate's opening debate

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: the opening of the word senate is its first letter

explanation.surface: A recording of the start of a Senate session in Washington.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to talk a matter over and argue its points.

clue.text: Line, say, written up at start of poem in exactly that way

indicators.note: the turned piece sits at the beginning of the poem word
in a down clue, written up means the letters are set upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means here
an ode is a lyric poem
sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as exactly as written

explanation.surface: A line of verse, quoted exactly, opens a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a geodesic is the shortest line between two points on a curved surface.

clue.text: One Conservative and another, much admired?

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
another means one more of each: another I for one and C for Conservative

explanation.surface: Two Tory politicians held up as heroes by admirers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something celebrated as a revered symbol or emblem of its kind.

clue.text: Anticipates announcement of what across rows in this puzzle contain

indicators.note: announcement says the phrase is spoken, so its sound gives the entry

parts.words: what across rows in this puzzle contain
parts.note: every across row in this grid holds four letter Cs

explanation.surface: A setter's note predicting what the grid's across entries will hold.
explanation.walkthrough: Count the Cs in each across row of the grid: there are four, and four Cs spoken aloud gives the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To foresee is to predict or expect something before it happens.

clue.text: Hundred mile races to be organised? It's a piece of cake

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: the letters are to be arranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hundred one-mile races to arrange? Easy as pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A piece of cake' tempts as meaning easy; here it is literal, a cake slice.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastry slice filled with cream, a literal portion of cake.

clue.text: Wild animal beginning to claw my back

indicators.note: the beginning of the word claw is its first letter
back means the exclamation is read backwards

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise like my!

explanation.surface: A creature starts to claw at the speaker's back.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for crocodile, a large wild reptile.

clue.text: Cleric's tarnished halo?

indicators.note: tarnished suggests damaged, so the letters are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A priest's halo has lost its shine.
explanation.definitionFit: A halo is a ring of light around a saint's head.

clue.text: Exotic dance with oddly cheesy rhythms

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange, so the letters are rearranged
oddly means take the odd-numbered letters of the word cheesy

explanation.surface: An unusual dance set to corny beats.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadences are rhythmic flows or modulations, as of speech or music.

clue.text: Plants must show compliance with laws about employment

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Plants must show compliance with laws about employment (8)': C + ACT(USE)S needs 'about' both as C (circa) and as the container round USE; no other word supplies the leading C, so a word does two jobs or the clue is misread
annotationWithheld.clue: Plants must show compliance with laws about employment

clue.text: Sport in play area on island folded

indicators.note: folded back means the whole run is turned around

parts.note: rec is short for recreation ground, a public playing field
Cos is a Greek island in the Dodecanese

explanation.surface: A game on a playing field on an island has been called off.
explanation.definitionFit: Association football, the sport played with a round ball.

clue.text: Crack about old knighted actor

parts.note: c, circa, means about
Sir Michael Caine is a knighted British film actor

explanation.surface: A drug scandal concerning an elderly film star with a title.
explanation.definitionFit: Crack is a smokable form of this drug.

clue.text: Commander, one wearing plain winter garment

indicators.note: wearing means the commander and one are put on inside the plain word

parts.note: overt means plain or open to view
CO is Commanding Officer
a means one

explanation.surface: An officer, one in plain clothes, wears something warm for winter.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy coat worn over other clothes in cold weather.

clue.text: Offender in prison drinks tea? You're joking!

indicators.note: drinks means the tea goes inside the offender

parts.note: nonce is British prison slang for a sex offender
cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: A convict sipping his tea is told it's out of the question.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation meaning not a hope, that will never happen.

clue.text: Wretched scoundrels caught in the act

indicators.note: the scoundrels are trapped inside the act

parts.note: act taken as written
curs are contemptible men, scoundrels

explanation.surface: Miserable villains were caught red-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurst means under a curse, hence wretched or doomed.

clue.text: A student in trouble kept quiet

indicators.note: trouble suggests disturbance, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A pupil in difficulty said nothing about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Not said aloud, left unspoken.

clue.text: Singer named Charles stops crooner doing asinine impersonation

indicators.note: stops means plugs, so one name fills a gap inside the other

parts.note: Bing Crosby was the famous American crooner
Ray Charles was the American soul singer

explanation.surface: One famous singer interrupts another's act of mimicry.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey's cry is a bray, so braying is imitating an ass.

clue.text: Chaotic hospital in charge of introducing a form of therapy

indicators.note: introducing means the therapy is put into the middle of the other letters

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital
IC means in charge
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy

explanation.surface: A frantic ward where the person in charge brings in electric shocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Frantic and busy, full of confused activity.

clue.text: Stood in front of class, perhaps, sounding tense

definitions.text: Stood in front of class, perhaps

indicators.note: sounding means the word heard is given, not its spelling

parts.note: taut means tense, stretched tight

explanation.surface: A nervous teacher standing at the front of the room.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher stands before a class and instructs it.

clue.text: Fight rifle carrier

parts.note: a ruck is a brawl or scrimmage
to sack is to plunder or rifle

explanation.surface: A soldier brawls over a gun bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A backpack used for carrying belongings.

clue.text: Russian ready to share a kiss?

parts.note: co- is a prefix meaning jointly or together, as when sharing
a peck is a quick kiss

explanation.surface: A Russian eager to exchange a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready is slang for cash, and a copeck is a Russian coin.

clue.text: Force thousands out of business

indicators.note: out of means the thousands are removed from the word

parts.note: commerce is trade or business
M is a thousand, so MM is thousands

explanation.surface: Pressure drives thousands out of trade.
explanation.definitionFit: To compel someone by pressure or threats.

clue.text: A clergyman's office near entrance to church? That's quite right

indicators.note: near means placed beside the other piece
the entrance of the word church is its first letter

parts.note: a curacy is the post held by a curate

explanation.surface: A vicar's office by the church door is approved.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the noun sense: being quite right is precision.
explanation.definitionFit: Correctness or precision, the state of being exactly right.

clue.text: Positioned fighter pilot between Poland and Germany

indicators.note: between means the pilot sits in the middle of the two countries

parts.note: PL is the international code for Poland
D is the international vehicle code for Germany
an ace is a top fighter pilot

explanation.surface: A war pilot was stationed between Poland and Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Put or set in a particular spot.

clue.text: Composer's timeless collection of records

indicators.note: without time, so the letter T for time is dropped

parts.note: a batch is a set or group, here of records

explanation.surface: A composer's ageless set of recordings.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Sebastian Bach, the German Baroque composer.

clue.text: Study chemistry, for example, showing diligence

parts.note: to con is to study or learn
chemistry is an example of a science

explanation.surface: Studying chemistry shows hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: Conscientiousness, scrupulous care in work.
